notes: Both coders gave both documents stance delegates. Of 45 matched units, most disagreements were on modality (informs vs should/may for descriptive or suggestion sentences; resolved by whether the sentence instructs anyone), phase (course-start/during-work/before-course for advice to instructors; resolved by when the action happens), and policy_type (P71 vs P81 for class-code reporting resolved to P71; P99 vs UNCOVERED for integrity reaffirmation resolved to UNCOVERED; P56 vs UNCOVERED for 'AI literacy is not about promoting AI use' resolved to UNCOVERED). unit_stance differences (restrict/encourage vs neutral) were resolved by whether the sentence takes a position on AI use. A found 14 extra units that were kept (extra assignment ideas, rationale and evidence sentences, split privacy/equity), B found 4 kept extras (survey evidence, Grammarly, a quote, update commitment); one A-only unit (a bare section title) was dropped. Matching is by anchor overlap or adjacency within the same sentence or passage; the A privacy and A hidden-tools units were left unmatched to B's neighbouring sentences.
